text: The rain jacket tip saved my commute. I arrived completely dry while everyone else looked like drowned rats.
name: Anna de Vries

text: Finally an app that tells me what to wear. No more freezing fingers on the Veluwe!
name: Joost Bakker

text: The ice warning stopped me from riding over a frozen bridge this morning. Thank you!
name: Marieke Jansen

text: I check the ride score before every training. My Sunday group now calls it 'the oracle'.
name: Pieter van Dijk

text: Wind gusts at the coast are no joke. This page predicted it better than my own legs.
name: Sanne Visser

text: Love the bike cleaning advice after a wet ride. My chain has never been happier.
name: Thomas Mulder

text: Simple, fast and no account needed. Exactly what a cyclist wants before leaving the house.
name: Lotte Smit

text: Dark in 2 hours? Good to know. I packed my lights and got home safely.
name: Ruben Meijer

text: The 'feels like' temperature is spot on. I finally dress for the wind instead of the thermometer.
name: Femke Hendriks

text: My kids check the ride score before school. Apparently a 9 means we cycle through the park.
name: Daan Kok

text: Foggy and cold? The warning made me swap to my bright lights. Best decision of the week.
name: Iris van den Berg

text: I used to guess the weather. Now I just open this page and go. Zero regrets, one dry saddle.
name: Bas Dekker

text: Wet autumn leaves warning? I slowed down in the corner and kept my skin on my knees.
name: Eva Brouwer

text: Great for my gravel rides. Knowing the rain of the last 6 hours tells me exactly how muddy the trail will be.
name: Niels de Boer

text: Not an official forecast, but better than my neighbour's knee. And much more polite.
name: Judith Peters

text: Sunglare warning on the way home? Never thought I'd need it, but there I was, squinting no more.
name: Koen Willems

text: Ten minutes of fresh data from a real KNMI station. This is how weather advice should work.
name: Lieke Hoekstra

text: Thunder alert kept me home. Ten minutes later the sky exploded. I'm still thankful.
name: Mark Scholten

text: Bike cleaning tips after the salted roads saved my drivetrain this winter.
name: Sophie Bos

text: The whole site loads instantly and knows where I am. I don't even know how, but I love it.
name: Tim Vermeulen

text: Perfect for the Zeeland dyke. Headwind going out, tailwind home. Planned the route around it.
name: Anouk Prins

text: Rule #5 on a rainy day? The page quoted The Rules at me and I harden-upped. Glad I did.
name: Gijs van Leeuwen

text: Seeing a Velominati rule next to the weather advice makes me smile every single morning.
name: Roos Kuipers

text: My club mates now argue over which of The Rules fits today's weather. This page started it.
name: Stefan Maas

text: The moon prediction is wild. Bright moon, clear sky: I rode without lights on the quiet dyke road and it was magical.
name: Merel Zijlstra

text: It knew the moon would be at 90% tonight. Best night ride of my life.
name: Wouter Lammers

text: Dark nights used to scare me. Now I check the moon illumination first and plan accordingly.
name: Noor Hermans

text: Clothing advice was spot on again: arm warmers off by 10 o'clock, exactly as predicted.
name: Vincent de Groot

text: Thermal gloves and overshoes, as suggested. Not a single cold toe all ride. Spot on!
name: Charlotte Kramer

text: I dressed exactly like the page said and was the only one in my group who was comfortable.
name: Floris Verhoeven

text: Score of 2 today, so I stayed home with a coffee. Ten minutes later it hailed. Best ride I never took.
name: Hanneke Dijkstra

text: The page said storm gusts and I believed it. Sofa day, zero regrets, still dry.
name: Robin Postma

text: Bad weather prediction? Then it's home trainer time. My FTP went up more this winter than ever.
name: Jasper Willemsen

text: Rain all morning, so I did two hours on the trainer. The ride score tells me when to stay inside.
name: Linda Smeets

text: My bike mechanic is happy: since I follow the cleaning advice, my chain lasts twice as long.
name: Henk Rademaker

text: Rinse after a wet ride, lube the chain. My mechanic called me his favourite customer.
name: Yara Mol

text: Thanks to the wet-drivetrain tips I skipped the expensive repair and saved up for a new bike instead. Delivery next week!
name: Dirk van Wijk

text: Less maintenance bills, more money in the new-bike jar. Cleaning the bike on time really pays off.
name: Esther Boer

text: I share a screenshot of my ride score in the club app every Saturday. Half the group now checks it before showing up.
name: Maarten Vos

text: One screenshot of the clothing advice and my whole WhatsApp group knew what to wear. Zero discussion for once.
name: Fleur Hoogland

text: Sent a screenshot of the ice warning to my dad. He stayed off the bike and called to say thanks.
name: Sven Mertens

text: The card looks great in a screenshot. My friends keep asking which app it is, and it's just a web page!
name: Tess Jacobs

text: I was a proper couch potato. The 'perfect ride' score got me out the door, and now I cycle three times a week.
name: Gerard Haan

text: Never cycled in winter. The clothing advice made it doable, and I lost 8 kilos since October!
name: Petra Vermeer

text: As a runner I was sceptical. Now I cross-train on the bike whenever the page says green. My knees thank you.
name: Mats Oosterhuis

text: From sofa to 40 km on Sundays. This page took away my excuse: 'I don't know what the weather will do'.
name: Ingrid Bosman

text: Triathlon training needs consistency. The ride score tells me which days to bike and which to swim.
name: Olaf Timmermans

text: Score below 10? That's my cue. Rain, wind, 5 degrees: 120 km on the road. Rule #9 says it all.
name: Bram Ketelaar

text: Everyone else sees a 6 out of 100 and stays inside. I see it as the official start signal for my long Sunday ride.
name: Hilde Vink

text: The worse the ride score, the longer I go. Last week: score 4, headwind, 150 km. Smiling the entire way home.
name: Jorrit Smits

text: I only do my long rides when the page says 'stay home'. Empty roads, full legs, and a very happy bike mechanic.
name: Marloes Kuiper

text: I used to dress like an Arctic explorer for a 10 degree ride and arrive soaked in sweat. Not anymore!
name: Karel Boersma

text: Always overdressed, always sweating. Now I wear exactly what the page suggests and I finally stay dry.
name: Annelies Vogel

text: Underdressed for years, shivering in the first 10 km every spring. These days I'm never cold anymore.
name: Rick Haasnoot

text: Shorts in March because 'the sun is out'. The page set me straight: knee warmers, and no more blue legs.
name: Nina Koster

text: I was the guy with three jackets in the backpack or none at all. Now I just get it right, every time.
name: Eric Dam

text: 18 weather parameters from a real KNMI station, updated every 10 minutes. No more guessing, the advice is simply correct.
name: Arjan Wolters

text: Wind chill, dew point, gusts, rain over the last 6 hours: the formulas behind this page are solid. I trust it more than any weather app.
name: Carla Brink

text: As a data nerd I checked the numbers against the KNMI station next door. They match to the decimal. Impressive.
name: Mischa Oudshoorn

text: It uses fresh measurements, not a forecast from yesterday. That's why it's right when the weather turns suddenly.
name: Bert Hofman

text: Since I follow this page I haven't been caught out by the weather once. The data is right, up to date, and local.
name: Willemijn Aarts

text: Score of 9 and sunshine, so I went out. Soaked within ten minutes. This site is a joke, I'm going back to Buienradar.
name: Hans Kleinjan

text: Bad predictions again: it said 'no rain jacket needed' and then it poured. Better look at Buienradar.
name: Cindy Rood

text: Wore what the page told me and froze anyway. Maybe the weather station is not on my street? Just saying.
name: Pim Hartog

text: Why do I need a 'ride score' when Buienradar just shows me the rain? Overcomplicated and wrong twice this week.
name: Greet Wijnands

text: Just look out of the window. That's free, instant and never wrong. Why do I need a website for that?
name: Ton Franken

text: I open the curtains and know exactly what to wear. No page needed, no score, no formulas.
name: Mieke Dorrestein

text: My grandfather felt the weather coming in his knee. This site is slower and less accurate.
name: Ruud Pothoven

text: You can feel it on your wooden shoes if it's going to rain. Nobody needs 18 parameters for that.
name: Klaas Bouwman

text: The formulas don't add up. It said 'feels like 4 degrees' and I was sweating like a pig on the first hill.
name: Dennis Ooms

text: Wind chill formula? Nonsense. Headwind was far worse than the page claimed. Check your maths.
name: Karin Tuinstra

text: The score was 8 out of 100 and it was a lovely ride. The formulas are off, completely.
name: Joep Lemmens

text: Cycling with a weather advice from KNMI data? That is another cook compared to guessing at the window. Completely different.
name: Ties Hoogeveen

text: Before I used this page, we were always running after the facts. Now the facts run after us, and the bike is dry.
name: Gerda Koopmans

text: It's a question of time before the rain comes. The page knows it, and I am home before it starts.
name: Evert Schouten

text: Every week the same song: wrong jacket, cold hands. Not with this page. Finally another song.
name: Marja Veldkamp

text: I rode without lights in the dark. That is not very smart, that can I say. The darkness warning would have told me.
name: Cor van Rijn

text: I believe that we can come to an end of cold fingers. With these gloves advice, it is only a question of one ride.
name: Sjoerd Kamphuis
